title: Ellington's superstitions
summary: They trade superstitions about buttons on the piano, shoes as gifts, fish and chips in English dressing rooms, and telegrams left up.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Do you remember any of his other superstitions?
Don't put any buttons on the piano keys, was one. Like if you had a button -- take a button off your
shirt or your coat, or something like that, don't put it on the piano keys. He wouldn't sit down there.
(Laughter.)
And let's see, I don't know what else. I can't -- I didn't stick that close with anyone.
I remember, never give anyone a present for their feet, socks or shoes or slippers.
Oh, yeah?
Because it means they're going to walk away from you.
Where did all these things come about?
Well, John Levy told me that's an old theatrical superstition. The first time I ever heard it was from Duke when a friend of his gave him a pair of slippers.
Yeah.
And he got very upset. He said, "Take them back, take them back. That means that you want me to walk away from you."
Well, the only thing I ever heard was the fish and chips in the dressing room, in England. And the peanuts, something about peanuts.
I don't know about those one.
I don't have any superstitions. I haven't got sense enough.
What was the superstition about fish and
You don't eat that in the dressing room in England. Bad luck, something. So --
I know -- (inaudible.)
I never take any cognizance with these things, because I don't believe in anything like that.

I know that he would put up his congratulatory messages and telegrams on opening night, and they couldn't be taken down, and they were to be left there when he left the premises; when he left the engagement, he'd leave them because it was bad luck to take them down.
My only superstition was I never got enough money.
(Laughter.)
Well, that's hardly a superstition.
I think we're at the end of this tape. (End of Reel Three.)
